chapter_theme: Siva as the sun (சிவாதித்தன்): his light of knowledge ends the darkness of bond and ignorance; he is in every body like the sun reflected in many pots, yet not confined by them; and he himself is the three lights, the gods, body and soul, and the elements.

2001.reading: The darkness of bond and the ignorance that stood against me vanished through the supreme light of Siva which is knowledge, as dense darkness leaves at the dawn where two lights become one.
2001.nuance: ஒன்றும் இருசுடர் ('the two lights that join') may be sun and moon at dawn or, as in chapter 144, the two breaths united. The main claim, that knowledge as Siva's light ends bond and ignorance, is plain.

2002.reading: When the sun appears in pot after pot, closing them does not shut him in; the poison-throated Lord who stands as though confined in the body he dwells in is of the same kind.
2002.nuance: The sun reflected in water-filled pots is a classic image for one presence in many bodies. Here the point is that Siva is in each body without being held by it; விடங்கொண்ட கண்டன் is Siva who swallowed the poison.

2003.reading: He himself is the spreading light that stands as the three lights in one; he himself establishes things, standing as Brahma and Vishnu; he himself stands not other than body and soul; he himself is open space, light and darkness.
2003.nuance: The fourfold தானே insists on one agent behind all. உடலுயிர் வேறன்றி ('not other than body and soul') states Siva's presence in them; how far it means identity is left open.

2004.reading: The divine lights, fire, sun and moon, the earth, water, fire, wind and sky, and the many souls the great Lord of the Saivas bears: these are the six limbs and the place, in between, for the five.
2004.nuance: The first three lines name Siva's traditional eight forms (the five elements, sun, moon and the soul), though fire is named twice. The last line, ஐவர்க்கு இடம் இடை ஆறங்கம், is obscure: ஐவர் may be the five deities and ஆறங்கம் six limbs (of the Veda, or six paths).

links.note: 2002 says Siva is in each body like the sun in many pots, not shut in by them; 2010 says he is in the soul and the soul in him, while being everywhere. Presence within without confinement, in two images.

source_issues: 2004 line 4 (ஐவர்க்கு இடம்இடை ஆறங்கம்) is obscure and may be corrupt.
